body.statement: Under the population dictionary, training measurability, conditional square-integrability, and bridge-rate conditions, the explicitly constructed fold dictionaries satisfy \[\max_k\|\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}-D^0_{J_n}\|_{L^2(P)}=O_p(\delta_{D,n}),\qquad \delta_{D,n}=O_p\{B_{J_n}(e_{h,4,n}+e_{q,4,n})+e_{h,4,n}e_{q,4,n}\}.\] Conditional on \(\mathcal D_{-k}\), training/holdout independence and the fourth-moment growth condition give \(\eta_{G,n}=O_p\{J_nB_{J_n}^2\sqrt{\log(1+J_n)/n}+\sqrt{J_n}B_{J_n}\delta_{D,n}+J_n\delta_{D,n}^2\}\) and \(\eta_{c,n}=O_p\{\sqrt{J_n}B_{J_n}^2\sqrt{\log(1+J_n)/n}+\sqrt{J_n}B_{J_n}\delta_{D,n}\}\). The positive ridge makes every fold coefficient unique, and resolvent perturbation gives \[\max_k\|\widehat b^{(-k)\top}\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0\|_2=O_p\!\left(\alpha_{J_n}+L_n\delta_{D,n}+\frac{\eta_{G,n}+\eta_{c,n}}{\kappa_{J_n}}+b_{\rho,n}\right)=o_p(1).\] The explicit deterministic coefficient-to-weight identity then yields \(\|\widehat\psi-\theta(P)-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\|_2=o_p(1)\); this convergence is derived rather than assumed.
body.justification: Ridge uniqueness and the deterministic four-corner affine conversion are valid and the exact perturbation equations identify the required controls.
body.gap: The stated primitive list omits multiplier envelopes, dimension-correct aggregation, same-training-sample concentration, and learned-coefficient factors in Gram-null-space perturbations.
body.consumer: Those controls must be added and verified before the affine ensemble is an implementable efficiency-attaining procedure.

obligation.what_is_open: Derive learned-dictionary and population-projection convergence for the displayed same-training-sample ridge construction from primitive, dimension-aware multiplier and Gram-null-space controls.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen fourth-norm bridge rates omit multiplier envelopes needed for cell-signal errors; coordinatewise rates aggregate with a square-root dimension factor in Euclidean vector norm; training--holdout independence does not concentrate a dictionary on its own training sample; and the empirical ridge equation introduces Gram-perturbation and ridge terms multiplied by the learned coefficient envelope in population-null directions.
obligation.attempted: I expanded every learned cell signal, aggregated its coordinate errors, and projected the empirical ridge normal equation onto the positive population Gram eigenspace. These calculations verify ridge uniqueness and the four-corner affine identity, while exhibiting the missing multiplier, dimension, dependence, and coefficient-envelope factors explicitly.
obligation.partial_result:
Two algebraic parts of the displayed construction are proved. First, since \(\rho_n>0\), every eigenvalue of
\(\widehat G^{(-k)}+\rho_n I\) is at least \(\rho_n\), so the ridge coefficient is unique. Second, direct collection of the pure and four-corner coefficients yields
\[
\sum_{j,\ell}\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}=1,
\qquad
\sum_a t_a\sum_{j,\ell}
\widehat\lambda_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}\widehat S_{a,j\ell}^{(-k)}
=\widehat B^{(-k)}-\widehat b^{(-k)\top}
\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}.
\]

The primitive-to-vector rate in the target does not follow from the listed assumptions. For one cell, writing
\(\Delta h=\widehat h-h^0\) and \(\Delta q=\widehat q-q^0\), exact expansion gives
\[
S_a(\widehat h,\widehat q)-S_a(h^0,q^0)
=(1-I_aq^0)\Delta h+I_a(Y-h^0)\Delta q-I_a\Delta q\Delta h.
\]
The first two terms require fourth-moment envelopes for
\(1-I_aq^0\) and \(I_a(Y-h^0)\), which are not consequences of an envelope on the population dictionary coordinates and \(\phi_0\). Moreover, even if every coordinate error were bounded by a common number \(d_n\), Euclidean aggregation gives only
\[
\|\widehat D_{J_n}^{(-k)}-D^0_{J_n}\|_{L^2(P;\ell^2)}
\le \sqrt{J_n}\,d_n,
\]
not the dimension-free bound asserted in the target.

There is a separate ridge-null-space obstruction. Put
\(G=E[D^0_{J_n}D_{J_n}^{0\top}]\),
\(c=E[D^0_{J_n}B^0]\), and let \(P_R\) project onto
\(\overline{\operatorname{range}}(G)\). Since
\(Gb_{J_n}=c\), the empirical ridge equation implies exactly
\[
G P_R(\widehat b-b_{J_n})
=P_R\{(\widehat c-c)-(\widehat G-G)\widehat b-\rho_n\widehat b\}.
\]
Inverting on the positive eigenspace therefore produces terms proportional to
\(\eta_{c,n}/\kappa_{J_n}\),
\(\eta_{G,n}\|\widehat b\|_2/\kappa_{J_n}\), and
\(\rho_n\|\widehat b\|_2/\kappa_{J_n}\). The affine-weight envelope can at most replace
\(\|\widehat b\|_2\) by a constant multiple of \(L_n\); it does not justify the target's dimension-free
\((\eta_{G,n}+\eta_{c,n})/\kappa_{J_n}\) bound or its ridge term involving only \(\|b_{J_n}\|_2\). Finally, training--holdout independence applies to held-out averages, not to a Gram matrix evaluated on the same training observations used to fit the dictionary. Thus the exact affine identity is valid, but the asserted learned projection convergence remains unproved under the frozen primitive list.
